Poisoned to Death

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Methyl Bromide used to exterminate Borer Beetles became the carrion of death, when lethal doses attacked the Ingrams in the comfort of their home. Who is to blame for the death of their 2 children?

Unique Selling Point:
On Friday the 21st of August, in a quiet suburban complex in Port Elizabeth, Selina and Stanton Ingram enjoyed the evening together with their children, twelve year old Tammy and seventeen year old Matthew. Little did they imagine that this would be the last time they would be together as a family. Unbeknownst to them they had been attacked by a lethal poison, Methyl Bromide, a substance well known to toxicologists but with no antidote. Stanton and Selina survived, but their children tragically didn’t. How did the poison get in?

Summary:
On Friday night of the 21st of August, the Ingram family had dinner with their twelve year old daughter Tammy, at their complex Apartment in Port Elizabeth. At around 8.30 pm their 17 year old son Matthew arrived home after having had dinner at a friend’s house. The family spent part of the evening together and then turned in for bed. Later that night the entire family started to get violently ill with vomiting and diarrhea. After trying to deal with the situation themselves it became obvious they needed emergency care and were rushed to the hospital by their eldest son Joshua. Selina and Stanton were so ill they were unable to take care of their children. At first they thought it was something they ate, but later realised it couldn’t have been that, as Matthew had not eaten with them. They were convinced they had some sort of a tummy bug.

On arrival at the hospital, the children were convulsing and because the doctors did not know what had caused them to be so ill, they put them both into an induced coma. This was after Matthew had been convulsing and frothing at the mouth in his brother’s arms, Tammy was convulsing continually. Stanton and Selina were too ill to take care of the children and they too were being treated in the hospital.

In the early hours of 23rd of August, Tammy passed away, whilst Matthew was still in an induced coma. The toxicology report from their blood tests showed that the family had high levels of the toxin Methyl Bromide in their blood stream, in Tammy and Matthew in fact so high that it was 10 times what is deemed a safe amount. The family were bewildered as they didn’t know how they could have inhaled this toxin.

Four weeks later, Matthew died in hospital, four days before his 18th birthday.


Further information:
After Tammy passed away a family friend, Mark Lola, went to their home and spoke to one of the neighbours about what had happened to Tammy, when she told him that Friday was the same day that Unit 21, one of five linked units in the complex that included the Ingram’s, had been fumigated for Borer beetle. The pesticide commonly used for exterminating Borer beetles is Methyl Bromide, which is banned in most first world countries, but South Africa is still in the process of phasing it out.

The neighbour also told Mark that the other three units including her own had been evacuated for the weekend, so why had the Ingrams not been told to evacuate?

Toxicologist Dr Gerard Verdoon says, it is the onus of the Pest Control Company, in this case a company called Pest Pro to follow the National guidelines when fumigating an area especially with such a toxic substance as Methyl Bromide. They have to inform all the people who might be affected, evacuate them for at least 8 hours after the toxin has been released and they have to put up signs informing people that a fumigation is taking place in the vicinity. In the case of the Ingrams they were not informed when the fumigation was taking place, they were not asked to evacuate, nor were any signs put out for people to be made aware of the fumigation.

So was this a case of oversight or total negligence? Carte Blanche investigates.

Morne du Preez, a neighbour who is willing to speak to Carte Blanche, tells the sequence of events before the tragic incident. He alleges that an Estate Agent Mannie Naicker from Affinity Real Estate informed them some time in July that Unit number 21 was going to be fumigated and that he and his other two neighbours would have to evacuate their premises.

At around the same time, Selina Ingram says she too was approached by the same Estate Agent and told this, but he said he didn’t know when the fumigation was going to happen, but he would let her know. She emphasised to him that she is a diabetic and he needs to tell her as she could get very ill. She never heard from the Estate agent Mannie Naicker again. Selina and Stanton’s unit is the last unit in the set of five units, they are number 18 and at the end.

In the mean time the other tenants from the other three units were asked to evacuate, but they were being a bit difficult because it was interfering with their work and their schedules, so on Sunday the 15th August, Mannie went to see Morne and Aidan the other neighbour and they agreed to a time for evacuation which would be the following week. The estate agent said that the attorney’s Greyvenstein had ordered this through the body corporate which is handled by Proficient Property’s Gary Hambury. They all agreed to the Friday as this wouldn’t interfere with their work schedules. Some of the neighbours were to be put up in a B&B but Morne chose to stay with his mother. In this meeting, Morne alleges that he and Aidan asked Mannie about unit 18 and shouldn’t they be evacuated as well, as the units all share a common firewall? Morne alleges that Mannie categorically said they weren’t going to get affected as they were too far away from the unit that was being fumigated. I have spoken to Aidan and he confirms this version of events. Morne, feels very bad about the situation, because he thought that the Ingrams had been told about the fumigation and were aware, so he didn’t think anything of it, and didn’t take it further by having a conversation about it with them. He feels guilty because if he had, then possibly the tragedy could have been averted. He emphasises that no signage had been put up in the complex warning people of the fumigation. They never met with the pest control company and there was no written communication to them from the body corporate. He also says the caretaker of the complex did not know the fumigation was happening, because had she known she would have warned people, apparently she is very good at that. In addition, when they returned on Saturday to stay in their apartments they were finding it hard to breathe so they had to leave and stay elsewhere until the fumes subsided. Apparently Methyl Bromide is odourless but they were still able to smell residue, which made them feel very ill. Aidan stayed at the complex on the Saturday night, but after they heard about Tammy’s death they moved out on the Sunday and stayed away for another two nights.

The Stanton’s are overwhelmed with grief and sorrow at the loss of their children, and appear to have been dearly loved by their church community and classmates, personal testimonies during the funerals were moving and very heart wrenching.

Dr Verdoorn the toxicologist says there are strict protocols that need to be adhered to when fumigating with Methyl Bromide, a Class 1a product, he has sent me those guidelines. According to the Ingrams and other neighbours at the complex most of the guidelines were not adhered to.

Protocols that needed to be followed by the Pest control company, had to come with an evacuation order and visible signage that warns people that a fumigation is in process. According to Aidan another neighbour, some notices were put out, but they were small and attached to the doors of the units that were being fumigated, they weren’t visible to other people in the complex unless they walked up to their doors.

Dr Verdoorn, is willing to talk about the effects of Methyl Bromide and in context of this case. Although I have not seen the toxicology report, according to Stanton Ingram the levels of Methyl Bromide were 10 times higher in the children than a safe amount. Dr Verdoorn says that is a crazy amount and says that the Pest Control Company should have a certificate that allows them to deal with this kind of toxin.

I have approached Pest Pro, Chris Inch is the owner with his father Desmond Inch, and Chris refused to answer any of my questions, he referred me to his lawyers but did not send me the number when requested, Gregory Clark And Associates. He says they are waiting for the results of the inquest, but that he had nothing more to say to me. I have not been able to ask if they have a certificate that allows them to work with Methyl Bromide.

I approached Mannie Naicker to see if he would give Carte Blanche an interview, but he refused and basically put the phone down on me. (call is recorded)

I then called Adri Pretorius the owner of Affinity Estate Agents and asked if she was willing to speak to Carte Blanche and explained to her that intern estate agent Naicker had put the phone down on me. At first she was quite cooperative, but challenged the facts of what both neighbours say that Mannie said as hearsay, that unit 18 wouldn’t be affected. She then said they had nothing to do with the appointment of the pest control company, that the pest control company was appointed by the seller. When I asked if she would mind approaching the seller to see if they would speak to Carte Blanche she became belligerent and told me to approach the seller myself and proceeded to end the conversation by putting the phone down on me.

The reality of this is that the estate agent was dealing with the tenants regarding the fumigation and when they had to evacuate the premises. The estate agent according to the Ingrams only contacted them once in July and never reverted to them regarding when the fumigation was to happen. The neighbours corroborate this by the fact that Mannie did tell them a week beforehand that unit 18 would not be affected and so need not be evacuated.

I tried calling the Managing agents and am trying to contact the body corporate representative, but have as yet not been able to get hold of them.

I have also not managed to contact the investigating officer, Warrant Officer Blom, from the Kabega Police station as yet. Not sure how relevant this is, other than the fact that a criminal case has been opened. (I am not sure against whom at this point)

Dr Neal Hendriks was the doctor that treated the family and Dr Britz was the neurologist. I have tried to contact Dr Hendriks regarding the toxicology report and if he is willing to speak about the condition of the children and the family when they arrived at the hospital, but as yet he has not returned my calls. He is in possession of the toxicology report, and the Ingrams don’t have a copy, as that one is with the police. I have also tried contacting Dr Britz, but as yet have not had a response. Stanton Ingram the father, has given me permission to contact the doctors.

The Ingram family is devastated, their eldest son Joshua is completely broken. Selina feels that her life has ended without her children, even though she is a devout Christian. Stanton Ingram’s faith in God appears to be what keeps him going, but he affirms that he lived his life for his children and now there is very little left to look forward to. Matthew had just been selected to be a prefect, and Tammy was about to celebrate her 13th birthday and go to high school. All their dreams for their children and their future have been shattered, so much so that they have basically packed up their house at Glenfield complex, they find it difficult to return there, let alone live in this place of sorrow.

Press Release:


A tragedy in Port Elizabeth cut short two young lives, a brother and sister, who were poisoned by a deadly toxic pesticide - during a fumigation of an apartment for sale, a few units away.

Script:


VO: Selina and Stanton Ingram have lived in this quiet suburban complex in Port Elizabeth with their two children, twelve year old Tammy //
Tammy: God is amazing because he listens to your prayer all the time.
VO: And seventeen year old Matthew for more than 10 years.//
Voice off camera: Best thing about lockdown
Tammy: Was spending time with my family.
VO: But tragedy struck this close knit family
Selena: We had such a special bond.Our souls are intertwined together.
VO: Friday night the 21st of August this year, was the beginning of the agonising deaths their children were to endure.

Stanton: When I came downstairs, Tammy was already having a fit. I grabbed her and she couldn't stop shaking and I just held her tight. I could hear the sound of fluid coming out of the mouth.

Selina: Matthew was such a hero, he was busy dying himself but he ran down, he got Tammy's gown,Tammy's slippers.

Stanton: We were so confused, so sick, It felt like you were suffocating, and the burning sensation and the nausea and you thinking of the kids and you can't help yourself

VO: The Ingrams' live in unit 18, at the end of a row of five duplexes. That night they were completely unaware they were breathing in a silent toxic killer.

Selina: The first thing I thought was food poisoning. And then I thought but Matthew didn't eat with us.

VO: A week earlier their neighbour Morne Du Preez from Unit 20 together with Unit 22 attended a meeting with Mannie Naicker from Affinity Real estate who was assisting with vacating arrangements due to a fumigation planned for Unit 21.

Morne: Manny Nicker came here on the 16th in the evening on the Sunday, it was agreed to then to do it on the Friday of the 21st of August.
Derek: Who agreed and who with?
Morne: It was the tenant at number 22. We agreed that we would go on the Friday and then the aunty next door, she was fine to go any time. then we asked the question, have you spoken to unit number 18?

VO: The neighbours voiced their concern as to why the Ingram’s unit wasn't being vacated as well, because the row of 5 houses shared a common ceiling.

Morne: And the words Manny Nicker said to us was that it's not necessary because they are too far away from the gas and the gas won't get to them.
Derek: Morne, do you remember that clearly?
Morne: Clearly.

LINK: This was Tammy's room, parents next door and Matthew's room at the end. But there's only one bathroom so while the children were being sick here, Stanton and Selena were also starting to feel ill and they were forced to go downstairs outside onto the lawn.

VO: By 2am the family was very ill, especially Tammy. Their eldest son Joshua and his wife rushed over and took them to Greenacres emergency .

Selina: I saw Matthew was foaming at the mouth, his eyes were just looking at nothing. And Joshua was begging Matthew not to die.

LINK: The doctors here at Green Acres hospital were totally perplexed. They just didn't know what was making the family so ill.

Hendricks: It was like nothing any of us have ever seen. These two children were seizuring uncontrolled. And the normal medication that would be given for the control of the seizures just didn't stop it.

VO: Dr Neil Hendricks a specialist physician and cardiologist, took over the management of the family in hospital. Both children had to be put on ventilators.

Hendricks: Their presentation didn't fit with an infectious agent So it was most likely a toxic agent.

Stanton: When the doctor saw me, he told me he couldn't hold back, he had to tell me Mister Ingram, I can't guarantee you that your daughter is going to make it through the night.

VO: Sadly, Tammy passed away in the early hours of Sunday morning whilst Matthew was still fighting for his life.

Stanton: When Tammy passed away the following morning, a very good family friend of ours went to the neighbours to tell them what had happened to us. And then they shared with him that Friday, there was a fumigation that took place, a few units from our unit, and all of them were vacated.

VO: Selina recalls being visited by intern agent Mannie Naicker a few weeks earlier.

Selena: He said they are going to do a fumigation for borer beetle, he gave me the names methyl bromide and naphthalene. His words were that he doesn't think it's going to reach us. So I asked him how lethal is this? And he said that it would kill you. And then he said he would let us know when this takes place. He gave me a business card
Derek: When was the fumigation discussed with you again?
Selina: Never:
Derek: By anyone?
Selena: Never.

LINK: The methyl bromide which seemingly permeated the ceiling is an odourless toxin used to exterminate borer beetle. It is lethal to humans, banned in most first world countries and still used in South Africa under stringent conditions. And there's no known antidote.

VO: The hospital ran blood tests for Methyl Bromide on both children and the concentration in their systems was well above the potentially hazardous benchmark of 50 milligrams per litre, Tammy's was recorded at 212 milligrams per litre.

Hendricks: When one looks at the levels of exposure that she's had, I don't think that we would be able to have saved her.

Stanton: So Matthew passed away the 18th of September, four weeks after Tammy passed away.

VO: Toxicologist Dr Gerhard Verdoorn is an expert in the use and control of pesticides and believes this tragedy could have been avoided.

Derek: Matthew's level was 179. Tammy's, 212. What does it say to you?
Gerhard: Absolutely lethal, lethal. There is no way they could have survived that Derek
Derek: The dad's level was 93
Gerhard: That's also getting to a level of being sub lethal, children have a much higher metabolism than adults so they are normally far more susceptible to a pesticide or a toxin.

VO: According to Dr Verdoorn, because the five units share a common ceiling, it is likely that the gas drifted from Unit 21 to 18. Once released, Methyl Bromide becomes gaseous and can penetrate walls, wood even cement.

Gerhard: So it goes into every place; a little hole in the ceiling, it goes in there.]It drifts all over the place and then it saturates the place.

LINK: Pest pro was the company appointed to carry out the fumigation of unit 21. But did they carry out all the required protocols to ensure that everybody in the area would be safe?

Gerhard: you've got to issue warnings to everybody in that particular building that the fumigation is bound to take place

VO: The Pest-control-operator regulations stipulate strict protocols for applying poisons like Methel Bromide. For example, the site needs to be inspected, and the affected area and surrounds need to be evacuated.

Gerhard: When you work with a highly hazardous substance, you have to put up a display board of 550 Square centimetres to say fumigation is taking place.

VO: We wanted some answers directly from Pestpro, as they hadn't responded to our questions.

Chris: I'm not there, there's nobody there and everything must be directed at my attorney.
VO: After our visit PestPro did respond in writing: and confirmed their registration, with the Department of Fishing and Forestry.

Gerhard: They should have the special wood inspection and fumigation specialisation as a pest control operator.

VO: Despite our request Pestpro has not supplied us with a valid certificate for that day's on site supervisor, co-owner, Chris Inch. The certificate we have seen was issued two months later.

Pestpro says they informed units 19, 20 and 22 in June about the fumigation and evacuation. They say they didn't evacuate the Ingram family based on their experience and on inspection of the structural layout, because, they say, the gas dosage was low and would not reach the upper level which they had taped closed, and as such unit 18 would not be affected.

Gerhard: You as a pest control operator have to take every precaution that there's no drift or spillover of the chemical into another part of the building or into the environment

VO: Pestpro states that on the day, all the required regulation methel bromide fumigation danger boards were taped on all the doors and windows of the vacated units.

Derek: Was there no signage around to say this is going to happen?
Morne: What I understand from Unit 22 is when he came in,he told me that there were no barriers around. There was nothing on the doors that I could see, there's no warning signs, no red tape somewhere.

Gerhard: The evidence is there, something went badly wrong in this case. It is the ultimate responsibility of the pest control operator.

VO: Pestpro adds that an email on 30 july from the estate agent dealing with the sale of unit 21, mentioned that Mrs Ingram had been made aware of the fumigation. As such the family had been advised.

According to Selina Ingram, in her meeting with the estate agent, he had promised to let her know the date. But neither he, nor Pestpro, ever did.

Stanton: That night when we were all sick here, our kids were dying, we didn't know that we were the only people in this whole row of units here.

VO: What is evident is that intern agent Mannie Naicker was central to the negotiations between all parties. He has refused to speak to us. Affinity Real Estate Principal Adri Pretorius responded and in summary states: That a fumigation is "standard procedure" when selling a unit and "any fumigation company must do their work with proper care and skill. No estate agency is responsible for fumigation." and that she elects not to be involved in a premature sensation driven broadcast around this tragedy.

VO: A criminal investigation is underway, charges are still to be determined, but nothing can bring back the fruitful and promising lives of Tammy and Matthew Ingram.

Stanton: We can hear their voices. We can hear their footsteps. We can feel them but they're not here. The rooms are empty. it's an empty space.
Selena: I just sit day and night and just think, my mind can't stop thinking about the children, the 'why', 'what if' and how much I need to be with them.

I have not been able to ask if they have a certificate that allows them to work with Methyl Bromide. Not sure how relevant this is, other than the fact that a criminal case has been opened. TX Details Back references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 06 December 2020 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 11 December 2020 Press Release: A tragedy in Port Elizabeth cut short two young lives, a brother and sister, who were poisoned by a deadly toxic pesticide - during a fumigation of an apartment for sale, a few units away. Script: VO: Selina and Stanton Ingram have lived in this quiet suburban complex in Port Elizabeth with their two children, twelve year old Tammy // Tammy: God is amazing because he listens to your prayer all the time. VO: And seventeen year old Matthew for more than 10 years.// Voice off camera: Best thing about lockdown Tammy: Was spending time with my family. VO: But tragedy struck this close knit family Selena: We had such a special bond.Our souls are intertwined together. VO: Friday night the 21st of August this year, was the beginning of the agonising deaths their children were to endure. Stanton: When I came downstairs, Tammy was already having a fit. I grabbed her and she couldn't stop shaking and I just held her tight. I could hear the sound of fluid coming out of the mouth. Selina: Matthew was such a hero, he was busy dying himself but he ran down, he got Tammy's gown,Tammy's slippers. Stanton: We were so confused, so sick, It felt like you were suffocating, and the burning sensation and the nausea and you thinking of the kids and you can't help yourself VO: The Ingrams' live in unit 18, at the end of a row of five duplexes. That night they were completely unaware they were breathing in a silent toxic killer. Selina: The first thing I thought was food poisoning. And then I thought but Matthew didn't eat with us. VO: A week earlier their neighbour Morne Du Preez from Unit 20 together with Unit 22 attended a meeting with Mannie Naicker from Affinity Real estate who was assisting with vacating arrangements due to a fumigation planned for Unit 21. Morne: Manny Nicker came here on the 16th in the evening on the Sunday, it was agreed to then to do it on the Friday of the 21st of August. Derek: Who agreed and who with? Morne: It was the tenant at number 22. We agreed that we would go on the Friday and then the aunty next door, she was fine to go any time. then we asked the question, have you spoken to unit number 18? VO: The neighbours voiced their concern as to why the Ingram’s unit wasn't being vacated as well, because the row of 5 houses shared a common ceiling. Morne: And the words Manny Nicker said to us was that it's not necessary because they are too far away from the gas and the gas won't get to them. Derek: Morne, do you remember that clearly? Morne: Clearly. LINK: This was Tammy's room, parents next door and Matthew's room at the end. But there's only one bathroom so while the children were being sick here, Stanton and Selena were also starting to feel ill and they were forced to go downstairs outside onto the lawn. VO: By 2am the family was very ill, especially Tammy. Their eldest son Joshua and his wife rushed over and took them to Greenacres emergency . Selina: I saw Matthew was foaming at the mouth, his eyes were just looking at nothing. And Joshua was begging Matthew not to die. LINK: The doctors here at Green Acres hospital were totally perplexed. They just didn't know what was making the family so ill. Hendricks: It was like nothing any of us have ever seen. These two children were seizuring uncontrolled. And the normal medication that would be given for the control of the seizures just didn't stop it. VO: Dr Neil Hendricks a specialist physician and cardiologist, took over the management of the family in hospital. Both children had to be put on ventilators. Hendricks: Their presentation didn't fit with an infectious agent So it was most likely a toxic agent. Stanton: When the doctor saw me, he told me he couldn't hold back, he had to tell me Mister Ingram, I can't guarantee you that your daughter is going to make it through the night. VO: Sadly, Tammy passed away in the early hours of Sunday morning whilst Matthew was still fighting for his life. Stanton: When Tammy passed away the following morning, a very good family friend of ours went to the neighbours to tell them what had happened to us. And then they shared with him that Friday, there was a fumigation that took place, a few units from our unit, and all of them were vacated. VO: Selina recalls being visited by intern agent Mannie Naicker a few weeks earlier. Selena: He said they are going to do a fumigation for borer beetle, he gave me the names methyl bromide and naphthalene. His words were that he doesn't think it's going to reach us. So I asked him how lethal is this? And he said that it would kill you. And then he said he would let us know when this takes place. He gave me a business card Derek: When was the fumigation discussed with you again? Selina: Never: Derek: By anyone? Selena: Never. LINK: The methyl bromide which seemingly permeated the ceiling is an odourless toxin used to exterminate borer beetle. It is lethal to humans, banned in most first world countries and still used in South Africa under stringent conditions. And there's no known antidote. VO: The hospital ran blood tests for Methyl Bromide on both children and the concentration in their systems was well above the potentially hazardous benchmark of 50 milligrams per litre, Tammy's was recorded at 212 milligrams per litre. Hendricks: When one looks at the levels of exposure that she's had, I don't think that we would be able to have saved her. Stanton: So Matthew passed away the 18th of September, four weeks after Tammy passed away. VO: Toxicologist Dr Gerhard Verdoorn is an expert in the use and control of pesticides and believes this tragedy could have been avoided. Derek: Matthew's level was 179. Tammy's, 212. What does it say to you? Gerhard: Absolutely lethal, lethal. There is no way they could have survived that Derek Derek: The dad's level was 93 Gerhard: That's also getting to a level of being sub lethal, children have a much higher metabolism than adults so they are normally far more susceptible to a pesticide or a toxin. VO: According to Dr Verdoorn, because the five units share a common ceiling, it is likely that the gas drifted from Unit 21 to 18. Once released, Methyl Bromide becomes gaseous and can penetrate walls, wood even cement. Gerhard: So it goes into every place; a little hole in the ceiling, it goes in there.]It drifts all over the place and then it saturates the place. LINK: Pest pro was the company appointed to carry out the fumigation of unit 21. But did they carry out all the required protocols to ensure that everybody in the area would be safe? Gerhard: you've got to issue warnings to everybody in that particular building that the fumigation is bound to take place VO: The Pest-control-operator regulations stipulate strict protocols for applying poisons like Methel Bromide. For example, the site needs to be inspected, and the affected area and surrounds need to be evacuated. Gerhard: When you work with a highly hazardous substance, you have to put up a display board of 550 Square centimetres to say fumigation is taking place. VO: We wanted some answers directly from Pestpro, as they hadn't responded to our questions. Chris: I'm not there, there's nobody there and everything must be directed at my attorney. VO: After our visit PestPro did respond in writing: and confirmed their registration, with the Department of Fishing and Forestry. Gerhard: They should have the special wood inspection and fumigation specialisation as a pest control operator. VO: Despite our request Pestpro has not supplied us with a valid certificate for that day's on site supervisor, co-owner, Chris Inch. The certificate we have seen was issued two months later. Pestpro says they informed units 19, 20 and 22 in June about the fumigation and evacuation. They say they didn't evacuate the Ingram family based on their experience and on inspection of the structural layout, because, they say, the gas dosage was low and would not reach the upper level which they had taped closed, and as such unit 18 would not be affected. Gerhard: You as a pest control operator have to take every precaution that there's no drift or spillover of the chemical into another part of the building or into the environment VO: Pestpro states that on the day, all the required regulation methel bromide fumigation danger boards were taped on all the doors and windows of the vacated units. Derek: Was there no signage around to say this is going to happen? Morne: What I understand from Unit 22 is when he came in,he told me that there were no barriers around. There was nothing on the doors that I could see, there's no warning signs, no red tape somewhere. Gerhard: The evidence is there, something went badly wrong in this case. It is the ultimate responsibility of the pest control operator. VO: Pestpro adds that an email on 30 july from the estate agent dealing with the sale of unit 21, mentioned that Mrs Ingram had been made aware of the fumigation. As such the family had been advised. According to Selina Ingram, in her meeting with the estate agent, he had promised to let her know the date. But neither he, nor Pestpro, ever did. Stanton: That night when we were all sick here, our kids were dying, we didn't know that we were the only people in this whole row of units here. VO: What is evident is that intern agent Mannie Naicker was central to the negotiations between all parties. He has refused to speak to us. Affinity Real Estate Principal Adri Pretorius responded and in summary states: That a fumigation is "standard procedure" when selling a unit and "any fumigation company must do their work with proper care and skill. No estate agency is responsible for fumigation." and that she elects not to be involved in a premature sensation driven broadcast around this tragedy. VO: A criminal investigation is underway, charges are still to be determined, but nothing can bring back the fruitful and promising lives of Tammy and Matthew Ingram. Stanton: We can hear their voices. We can hear their footsteps. We can feel them but they're not here. The rooms are empty. it's an empty space. Selena: I just sit day and night and just think, my mind can't stop thinking about the children, the 'why', 'what if' and how much I need to be with them.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Methyl Bromide used to exterminate Borer Beetles became the carrion of death, when lethal doses attacked the Ingrams in the comfort of their home. Who is to blame for the death of their 2 children?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: On Friday the 21st of August, in a quiet suburban complex in Port Elizabeth, Selina and Stanton Ingram enjoyed the evening together with their children, twelve year old Tammy and seventeen year old Matthew. Little did they imagine that this would be the last time they would be together as a family. Unbeknownst to them they had been attacked by a lethal poison, Methyl Bromide, a substance well known to toxicologists but with no antidote. Stanton and Selina survived, but their children tragically didn’t. How did the poison get in?
metadata.Summary: On Friday night of the 21st of August, the Ingram family had dinner with their twelve year old daughter Tammy, at their complex Apartment in Port Elizabeth. At around 8.30 pm their 17 year old son Matthew arrived home after having had dinner at a friend’s house. The family spent part of the evening together and then turned in for bed. Later that night the entire family started to get violently ill with vomiting and diarrhea. After trying to deal with the situation themselves it became obvious they needed emergency care and were rushed to the hospital by their eldest son Joshua. Selina and Stanton were so ill they were unable to take care of their children. At first they thought it was something they ate, but later realised it couldn’t have been that, as Matthew had not eaten with them. They were convinced they had some sort of a tummy bug. On arrival at the hospital, the children were convulsing and because the doctors did not know what had caused them to be so ill, they put them both into an induced coma. This was after Matthew had been convulsing and frothing at the mouth in his brother’s arms, Tammy was convulsing continually. Stanton and Selina were too ill to take care of the children and they too were being treated in the hospital. In the early hours of 23rd of August, Tammy passed away, whilst Matthew was still in an induced coma. The toxicology report from their blood tests showed that the family had high levels of the toxin Methyl Bromide in their blood stream, in Tammy and Matthew in fact so high that it was 10 times what is deemed a safe amount. The family were bewildered as they didn’t know how they could have inhaled this toxin. Four weeks later, Matthew died in hospital, four days before his 18th birthday.
metadata.Further information: After Tammy passed away a family friend, Mark Lola, went to their home and spoke to one of the neighbours about what had happened to Tammy, when she told him that Friday was the same day that Unit 21, one of five linked units in the complex that included the Ingram’s, had been fumigated for Borer beetle. The pesticide commonly used for exterminating Borer beetles is Methyl Bromide, which is banned in most first world countries, but South Africa is still in the process of phasing it out. The neighbour also told Mark that the other three units including her own had been evacuated for the weekend, so why had the Ingrams not been told to evacuate? Toxicologist Dr Gerard Verdoon says, it is the onus of the Pest Control Company, in this case a company called Pest Pro to follow the National guidelines when fumigating an area especially with such a toxic substance as Methyl Bromide. They have to inform all the people who might be affected, evacuate them for at least 8 hours after the toxin has been released and they have to put up signs informing people that a fumigation is taking place in the vicinity. In the case of the Ingrams they were not informed when the fumigation was taking place, they were not asked to evacuate, nor were any signs put out for people to be made aware of the fumigation. So was this a case of oversight or total negligence? Carte Blanche investigates. Morne du Preez, a neighbour who is willing to speak to Carte Blanche, tells the sequence of events before the tragic incident. He alleges that an Estate Agent Mannie Naicker from Affinity Real Estate informed them some time in July that Unit number 21 was going to be fumigated and that he and his other two neighbours would have to evacuate their premises. At around the same time, Selina Ingram says she too was approached by the same Estate Agent and told this, but he said he didn’t know when the fumigation was going to happen, but he would let her know. She emphasised to him that she is a diabetic and he needs to tell her as she could get very ill. She never heard from the Estate agent Mannie Naicker again. Selina and Stanton’s unit is the last unit in the set of five units, they are number 18 and at the end. In the mean time the other tenants from the other three units were asked to evacuate, but they were being a bit difficult because it was interfering with their work and their schedules, so on Sunday the 15th August, Mannie went to see Morne and Aidan the other neighbour and they agreed to a time for evacuation which would be the following week. The estate agent said that the attorney’s Greyvenstein had ordered this through the body corporate which is handled by Proficient Property’s Gary Hambury. Morne alleges that Mannie categorically said they weren’t going to get affected as they were too far away from the unit that was being fumigated. I have spoken to Aidan and he confirms this version of events. Morne, feels very bad about the situation, because he thought that the Ingrams had been told about the fumigation and were aware, so he didn’t think anything of it, and didn’t take it further by having a conversation about it with them.
